Read /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000/WORKFLOW-PLAN.md first: it lists every evidence file, the tools and the facts already established. Evidence root: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000. Source tree: /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf
(engine C++ under src/, CN Rust under experimental/starrocks/src, translator under experimental/starrocks/crates/starrocks-plan-translator, StarRocks FE Java under experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe).
Key pre-digested files: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000/results.md (timings per arm), /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000/survey/plan-summary.txt and /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000/survey/explain/qNN.costs.txt (FE plans), /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000/card-compare-cn1.txt and card-compare-cn4.txt (FE estimate vs actual rows per exchange),
/tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000/cn1-cnlog.txt / cn4-cnlog.txt (+ .json: per run fragments, declared cardinalities, nixl transmits, OOM reschedules), /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000/cn1-quent.txt / cn4-quent.txt / standalone-quent.txt (+ .json: task state time, reservation vs peak, batches, dwell, staging leases),
/tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000/cn1-ops.txt etc (per-operator Computing time), /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000/standalone/runs/qNN.explain.txt (DuckDB/Sirius plan of the same SQL), /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000/cn1/dump/ (FE fragment params + Substrait per fragment), /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000/compare-*.txt (oracle correctness).
You may run the python tools in /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000 and read the source; do not modify the source tree, do not start clusters or GPU jobs (they are exclusive resources owned by the orchestrator), do not write outside /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000/agent-notes/.
The three focus dimensions are: (A) query planning, (B) cardinality estimation, (C) backpressure (memory pressure, parked intermediates, staging leases, queue waits, OOM reschedules, scaling 1->4 CN).
Every finding must cite concrete evidence (file + the line or number) and, where it proposes a change, name the file/function and rate confidence. Distinguish measured facts from inference.

Refute this finding FROM THE SOURCE: read the code paths it names (and the ones it should have named) in the engine, CN and FE, and check whether the mechanism claimed is what the code does, whether the proposed change is feasible where it is proposed, and whether an existing knob or code path already covers it. Default to refuted=true only with a concrete code-level contradiction.

Finding under test (from analyst "oom-failures"):
{
 "id": "OOM-2",
 "dimension": "backpressure",
 "claim": "The receiver-first rendezvous plus one-fragment-at-a-time engine thread turn every exchange into a full GPU materialisation: a sender runs to completion and parks its whole output, and a receiver is only planned/built after all its senders finished, so nothing streams across a fragment boundary. In q05 the lineitem sender ran alone with the entire 100 GiB pool and still filled it with its own output in 1.3 s.",
 "evidence": [
  "cn1/cluster.log 13:03:43.375-13:05:24.632: q05 fragments run strictly sequentially: nation ...5771 (6 ms), region ...5770 (9 ms), lineitem ...5774 started 13:03:43.433 and failed 13:05:24.627 (elapsed_ms=101193); supplier/customer/orders/join fragments start only after the failure; all 11 exec_plan_fragment RPCs had arrived by 13:03:43.462",
  "Quent data_batch Stationary events (cn1/quent/.cn0/*/data_batch) between 13:03:43.433 and the first OOM 13:03:44.795: 39 batches x 2.67 GB = 104.06 GB parked, cum 24.0 GB at +0.32 s, 66.7 GB at +0.88 s, 104.1 GB at +1.32 s; first OOM line: `global usage 107374182400 bytes (102400.00 MB), peak allocated 3376381184, reservation 3318948864` (engine-cn0.log 13:03:44.795)",
  "cn1-quent.txt q05.r0 ...5774: STREAMING_SINK n=40 in=104.30GB, dwell_max=101.0 s (batches never consumed); receiver ...5775 wall=184.5 s with Comp=0.128 s (its output parked waiting for the join-10 fragment that never started)",
  "engine.rs:278-280 'One request at a time until the handle is dropped'; engine.rs:697-716 park after `fragment.run()`; engine.rs:610-644 relay_from runs after build() of the receiver; sirius_ffi.cpp:739-745 relay_from throws unless the source fragment has run; local_exchange.rs:248-283 take_ready requires every expected sender complete",
  "Same arithmetic for the others (engine-cn0.log [gpu_pool] allocated): q18 own senders parked customer 3.94 + agg ~24 + orders 36.75 = 64.7 GB before the lineitem sender got 35.87 GB (End 104.42 GB @13:14:56.804); q21 first lineitem scan parked 77.76 GB (Begin 77.76 GB @13:16:15.274) before the second got 25.37 GB"
 ],
 "impact": "Any query whose fragment cut ships more than (pool - already parked) bytes through one exchange is infeasible on a CN, independent of how fast the operators are; at SF1000 that is every unfiltered lineitem exchange (97-245 GB) and, on 4 CNs, still ~25-61 GB per CN of lineitem plus the other parked streams.",
 "confidence": "high",
 "code_refs": [
  "experimental/starrocks/src/engine.rs:278-300,486-720 (run_fragment_inner: declare, build, relay_from, run, park)",
  "experimental/starrocks/src/local_exchange.rs:1-70,248-283 (SenderSource::LocalParked, take_ready)",
  "src/sirius_ffi.cpp:727-790 (Fragment::relay_from), src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:95-118"
 ],
 "proposed_change": "Streaming receivers: let a receiver fragment build once its build-side streams are complete and consume probe-side streams while the sender is still producing (bounded queue between STREAMING_SINK and STREAMING_SOURCE inside the same engine instead of park-then-relay), and run sender and receiver concurrently on the engine thread pool. That alone would make q17 (lineitem is the FE's probe side of exchange 1) runnable; for q05/q08/q09/q18/q21 the FE puts lineitem on the build side, so it must be combined with OOM-1 (stats) or a translator build/probe swap. Confidence: high on the mechanism, medium on the design.",
 "queries": [
  "q05",
  "q08",
  "q09",
  "q17",
  "q18",
  "q21"
 ],
 "family": "oom-failures"
}

Return refuted=true/false with your reasoning, corrections to the claim or numbers if any, and extra evidence you found.

# SF1000 profiling: planning / cardinality / backpressure — evidence bundle and analysis plan

Build: worktree /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf, branch perf/profile-sf1000 = d24f02c4 + 85658f09 (aggregate gate) +
9a5a4da6 (async sender dispatch) + 45dab3be (Quent probes: scan_split_read, stream hops, staging leases, CN fragment labels).
Data: /scratch/sirius/datasets/tpch_sf1000 (decimal TPC-H, one parquet dir per table). Queries: experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries/qNN.sql.

## Evidence (scratchpad = /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000)
- survey/explain/qNN.costs.txt, qNN.verbose.txt   FE EXPLAIN COSTS / VERBOSE for all 22 queries (fragments, join distribution, cardinality: 1 everywhere)
- survey/plan-summary.txt                          explain_summary.py over all 22 (joins with build/probe children and broadcast tables)
- cn1/  cn4/  standalone/                           the three arms; each has runs/runs.csv (query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc), runs/qNN.rK.out(.err)
- cn1/cluster.log, cn4/cluster.log                  FE + CN logs (fragment run started/finished, declared input stream cardinality, relayed batches, transmitted batches via nixl, OOM reschedule warnings)
- cn1/dump/fragment-*.txt, plan-*.substrait         every fragment the FE sent to the 1-CN and the translator's Substrait plan
- cn1/quent/.cnN/<session>/, cn4/quent/.cnN/<session>/, standalone/quent/<session>/   Quent ndjson (task FSM, data_batch, batch_placement, memory, scan_split_read)
- standalone/runs/qNN.explain.txt                   DuckDB/Sirius EXPLAIN of the same SQL (the stats-aware planner's choice)
- <arm>-cnlog.json (cnlog_extract.py), <arm>-quent.txt / .json (quent_bp.py), card-compare-<arm>.txt (card_compare.py), results.md (results_table.py)
- ../../oracle/tpch_sf1000/qNN.tsv                  DuckDB CPU oracle answers; compare-*.txt

## Tools (same dir)
explain_summary.py, cnlog_extract.py, card_compare.py, quent_bp.py, results_table.py, ../quent_summary.py (per-operator Computing sums)

## Facts established before the analysis
1. FE StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode sets outputRowCount = 1 for FILES() scans ("we don't know the real schema in file, just use the default Row Count now"); every column statistic UNKNOWN. Hence every plan node has cardinality 1 and the CBO picks BROADCAST for most joins (orders 1.5B rows broadcast in q07/q09/q10..., lineitem 3.79B rows as the build side of q04's LEFT SEMI JOIN, partsupp 800M in q02).
2. Engine stream ids == FE exchange node ids; the receiver declares the exact parked row count per stream before build() ("declared input stream cardinality"), so DuckDB plans the receiver fragment with exact input cardinalities, but only after every sender finished (receiver-first rendezvous, local_exchange.rs). Nothing streams across a fragment boundary: the whole intermediate is parked on the GPU.
3. Engine OOM handling: gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp reschedules a task on OOM up to MAX_RETRIES=100 with a 50 ms sleep, then fails the query ("exceeded maximum retry limit"). It does not wait for memory to be released and cannot spill parked batches. q05 and q08 died this way on 1 CN at SF1000 (GPU_SCAN OOM, 101 s and 168 s).
4. Reserving.requested_bytes / peak_estimate vs Computing.peak_allocated_bytes (Quent task FSM) measure the engine's own memory estimation; standalone SF10 q01 requested 20.8 GB for a 5.6 GB peak.

## Analysis dimensions (workflow)
A. Planning: per query, FE fragment tree and join distribution vs the DuckDB/Sirius standalone plan; what a stats-aware FE would choose; where the translator/CN could override (e.g. swap build/probe, refuse broadcast above a row threshold, local re-planning of a broadcast join once the actual parked cardinality is known).
B. Cardinality: FE estimate vs actual rows per exchange (card_compare), engine reservation estimate vs peak (quent_bp), the receiver-first exact-cardinality mechanism and its cost.
C. Backpressure: parked bytes and dwell per fragment, staging lease held/in-transit time and max concurrency vs SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES, Reserving/Queued waits, OOM reschedule storms, nixl transmit lease_ms/write_ms, 1-CN vs 4-CN scaling per query, standalone vs CN.
Each per-query analysis is verified adversarially (two skeptics with different lenses); the synthesis ranks findings with the evidence lines and proposes changes with file paths and confidence.

## Facts added after the 1-CN sweep (13:19 UTC)
5. Supported on the CN path at SF1000 (1 CN, 100 GiB pool): q01 q02 q03 q04 q06 q07 q10 q11 q12 q13 q14 q15 q19 q20 q22 pass (15). Fail: q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 = OOM at GPU_SCAN after 100 reschedules
   (101 s, 168 s, 232 s, 104 s, 54 s, 114 s to die; 2500-5600 reschedule warnings each, see cn1-cnlog.txt); q16 = translator gap ("multi_distinct_count has a partial state this translator does not model").
6. q15 returned 0 rows in run 1 and 1 row in runs 0 and 2 on 1 CN: streams 18 and 22 (the revenue = max(revenue) join output) carried 0 rows in run 1 while every other stream was identical.
   The build has the canonical float-sum sort gated OFF (SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS unset), so the two independently computed FP64 sums can differ in the last bits. Follow-up arms cn1-canon-q15 / cn1-nocanon-q15 test this.
7. Engine executor pools default to pipeline num_threads: 4 (docs/super-sirius/configuration.md:91-94); Quent "Queued" time per fragment is the wait for one of those slots plus the memory reservation gate.
   1-CN q04: scan fragment 37 tasks, Queued sum 19.9 s vs Computing 4.7 s inside a 1.2 s wall; join fragment requested 253 GB of reservations for a 61 GB summed peak (4x over-estimate).
8. Translator comment (node_translator.rs ~1924-1931) already records that the FE reports cardinality 1 for every FILES() scan and that nothing bounds a join build side; "bounding it belongs to the executor".
9. FE plans with 4 CNs alive are in survey/explain4/ (plan-summary-4cn.txt); diff against plan-summary.txt shows whether node count changes any distribution decision.
10. Plan-node enum decode for the dumps (TPlanNodeType(N)): survey/TPlanNodeType.map.txt (4 HASH_JOIN, 6 AGGREGATION, 8 SORT, 9 EXCHANGE, 17 FILE_SCAN, 28 PROJECT, ...).
11. The engine's DuckDB optimizer runs on every fragment (sirius_ffi.cpp:135, with STATISTICS_PROPAGATION and a few rewrites disabled, :233-240); the declared stream cardinality feeds the TableFunction cardinality callback (stream_bind_catalog.hpp:44-46), so build/probe choice inside a fragment sees exact stream sizes, but FILES() scans inside the same fragment carry DuckDB's parquet estimate. The FE's fragment cut (what is broadcast/shuffled) is fixed before any of this.
12. The FE's plan DEPENDS on the number of alive CNs even with cardinality 1 everywhere: with 4 CNs most joins flip from BROADCAST to PARTITIONED (shuffle) and fragment counts rise (q02 13->16, q08 11->16, q09 9->12; q03 orders join BROADCAST->PARTITIONED; q04/q12/q14/q19 BROADCAST->PARTITIONED; q15 -> BUCKET_SHUFFLE). survey/plan-summary.txt (1 CN) vs survey/plan-summary-4cn.txt (4 CNs); card-compare-cn4.txt uses the 4-CN plans (q03 exch2 = 3.23B lineitem rows shuffled, q12 exch1 = 1.5B orders rows shuffled).
13. 4-CN staging leases per query (cn4-quent.txt, attributed by time): q07.r1 747 leases / 141.5 GB moved / 92.9 s summed lease-held time inside a 1.79 s query, max 64 concurrent leases per CN; q04.r1 360 leases / 48.8 GB; q01.r1 14 leases / 0.06 GB. Session-wide per CN ~3700 leases, max 94 concurrent (arena = 16 GiB).
14. Standalone (one GPU, 100 GiB pool, DuckDB planner with parquet statistics) runs the same 15 queries; standalone/runs/qNN.explain.txt holds its plans. 1-CN vs standalone warm medians (ms): q01 5073/4882, q02 1246/571, q03 3106/3050, q07 3476/3266, q11 970/336, q15 4685/2627, q20 4171/3023, q22 943/496 (results.md).
15. Pre-digested tables added: reservation-ratio.txt (per run: tasks, summed reservation request vs summed measured peak, ratio, summed Queued and Computing seconds, wall; cn1 q11 54x, q14 15x, q03 14x, q10 6x over-reservation), cn4-transmits.txt (nixl transmits per run: count, GB, elapsed/lease/write ms, write GB/s).
16. Correctness vs the DuckDB oracle (compare-cn1.txt, compare-cn4.txt, compare-standalone.txt; rel tol 1e-6): standalone 15/15 MATCH. CN arms: q02 q04 q06 q12 q13 q14 q20 q22 MATCH; q01 q07 q19 differ by 9.6e-4 and q03 by 1.8e-3 in revenue sums (the known `1 - 0.07` FP64->DECIMAL(16,2) truncation from #1236's lowering, not a multi-CN defect); q10 differs with maxreldiff 12.3 over 48 cells of its 20 rows, most likely the same truncated revenue sums reordering the TOP-20 (verify by comparing the customer sets and the revenue column); q15 differs by 1.1e-3 on its single row and is also flaky in row count (see fact 6); q11 shows EMPTY because the query returns 0 rows at SF1000 on both engines (the bench kit does not scale q11's 0.0001 fraction by 1/SF), so it is not a defect but the compare cannot confirm it.
17. results-ratios.md: 1-CN parity T_sr1/T_standalone is 0.95-1.2 for the scan-heavy queries (q01 q03 q04 q06 q07 q12 q14 q19), 1.2-1.4 for q10 q13 q20, and 1.8-2.9 for the fragment-heavy small ones (q02 2.18, q11 2.88, q15 1.78, q22 1.90); 4-CN speed-up over 1 CN is 1.7-2.35x (efficiency 0.43-0.59) for the scan-heavy queries and 1.08-1.46x for q02 q11 q22.
18. Follow-up arms (may still be running while you work; use them only if their files exist): standalone-failed/runs/runs.csv (standalone Sirius on q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21), cn1-canon-q15/runs/runs.csv (1 CN, SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS=1, 6 runs of q15) vs cn1-nocanon-q15/runs/runs.csv (gate off).
19. DONE: standalone Sirius (same GPU, same 100 GiB pool, DuckDB planner with parquet statistics, pipelined execution) runs every query the CN path could not: q05 5191/2786 ms (pass, rows=5), q08 3835/3674 ms (pass, rows=2), q09 6818/5427 ms (pass, rows=175), q17 4386/3786 ms (pass, rows=1), q18 2764/2691 ms (pass, rows=100), q21 6534/6401 ms (pass, rows=100) (cold/warm; standalone-failed/runs/runs.csv, plans in standalone-failed/runs/qNN.explain.txt, Quent in standalone-failed/quent/). The CN path died on the same queries after 54-232 s of OOM reschedules. This is the central planning + backpressure contrast of the campaign.
20. DONE q15 determinism A/B on 1 CN (6 runs each): SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS=1 -> rows per run ['0', '1', '0', '0', '1', '0'] (ms ['10331', '5161', '5182', '5002', '4876', '4809']); gate off -> rows ['0', '0', '1', '0', '0', '0'] (ms ['10576', '4795', '4847', '4799', '4661', '4788']). Files: cn1-canon-q15/, cn1-nocanon-q15/ (runs, cluster.log, quent, engine-*.log).
21. CORRECTION to fact 6: the A/B in fact 20 REFUTES the simple hypothesis that the SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS gate alone explains q15's empty runs: with the canonical sort ON, 4 of 6 runs still return 0 rows (gate off: 5 of 6). The gate only canonicalizes row order inside the update-phase aggregate; the FE plan computes the revenue CTE twice (two independent two-phase aggregations over FP64-lowered decimals) and then joins on `total_revenue = max(total_revenue)`. Batch arrival order into the merge phase (and therefore FP64 summation order) still varies run to run, so the two sums can differ in the last bits and the equality join yields nothing. Standalone Sirius keeps DECIMAL and returns the row every time. Treat this as a correctness finding about equality joins on FP64-lowered aggregates on the CN path; verify from cn1-canon-q15/ and cn1-nocanon-q15/ logs (declared cardinalities of streams 18/22 per run) and the translator's decimal->FP64 lowering (#1236, cast_to_fp64 in expr_translator.rs).
22. compare-standalone-failed.txt: standalone results for q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 vs the DuckDB oracle: q05=MATCH q08=MATCH q09=MATCH q17=MATCH q18=MATCH q21=MATCH

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Quent-instrumented CN capture at SF1000. usage: capture-cn.sh <num_cns> <tag> <timeout_s> <runs_after_warmup> q01 q03 ...
# Cluster: 100GiB GPU pool, 16GiB staging, 160GiB host per CN (the perf plan's retime configuration), watchdog 300 s,
# Quent on with per-fragment labels, async sender dispatch on. Telemetry dirs are wiped before launch so the newest
# session per CN is this arm's; after a clean SIGTERM the sessions are copied to <out>/quent/cn<i>/.
SP=/tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad
WT=/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf; SR=$WT/experimental/starrocks; DATA=/scratch/sirius/datasets/tpch_sf1000
N=$1; TAG=$2; TO=$3; RUNS=$4; shift 4
OUT=$SP/perf/sf1000/$TAG; mkdir -p $OUT/quent
source $SP/cluster-env.sh $WT
export NUM_CNS=$N GPU_MEM=100GiB HOST_MEM=160GiB STAGING=16GiB SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES=16GiB SIRIUS_QUERY_WATCHDOG_SECS=300
export SIRIUS_CN_ENABLE_QUENT=1 SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1
[ "$N" = 1 ] && { export SIRIUS_CN_DUMP_FRAGMENTS=$OUT/dump; mkdir -p $OUT/dump; rm -f $OUT/dump/*; }
M="mysql --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9030 --user root --batch --connect-timeout=5"
echo "##### CAPTURE $TAG NUM_CNS=$N queries: $* $(date -u +%T)"
pgrep -f "$SR/target/release/sirius-starrocks-cn" >/dev/null && { echo "REFUSING: CNs from this worktree still running"; exit 2; }
rm -rf $SR/.cn*/telemetry/*
bash $SP/start-cluster.sh $WT $OUT/cluster.log
for i in $(seq 1 60); do n=$($M -e "SHOW COMPUTE NODES;" 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="Alive") c=i; next} $c=="true"{n++} END{print n+0}'); [ "$n" = "$N" ] && break; sleep 3; done
echo "alive=$n after $((i*3))s"; nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.used --format=csv,noheader | tr '\n' ' '; echo
bash $SP/perf/sf1000/run-queries.sh $TAG $DATA $OUT/runs $TO $RUNS "$@"
echo "== stopping (SIGTERM, wait) $(date -u +%T)"; bash $SP/stop-cluster.sh $WT
for d in $SR/.cn*; do cn=$(basename $d); [ -d $d/telemetry ] || continue; for s in $d/telemetry/*/; do mkdir -p $OUT/quent/$cn; cp -r $s $OUT/quent/$cn/; done; done
grep -a "/\* $TAG " $SR/starrocks/output/fe/log/fe.audit.log 2>/dev/null | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' > $OUT/fe.audit.$TAG.log
echo "audit lines with marker: $(wc -l < $OUT/fe.audit.$TAG.log); quent sessions: $(ls -d $OUT/quent/*/*/ 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"
echo "##### CAPTURE $TAG DONE $(date -u +%T)"

89:Conversions that land data on the HOST tier draw down a caller-owned reservation instead of double-committing host capacity: the caller obtains a reservation with `make_reservation_or_null(size)` and passes it to the reservation-taking `convert_to`/`clone_to` overloads, so the converter's allocation is charged against capacity the caller already holds. If the reservation cannot be made, the call falls back — with a warning — to the `memory_space*` overload (no reservation; the converter may OOM). Call sites: `lock_or_prepare_batch` in `src/include/pipeline/batch_lock_utils.hpp` and the materialized result collector (`src/op/sirius_physical_result_collector.cpp`). The `memory_space*` overloads remain the path for GPU/DISK targets and viability probes.
91:## Downgrade Executor
93:**File:** `src/include/downgrade/downgrade_executor.hpp`, `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp`
95:One `downgrade_executor` per memory space monitors pressure and moves data to lower tiers.
99:- **Processing thread**: dequeues `downgrade_request` objects sequentially from an `interruptible_mpmc` queue
100:- **Monitor thread** (if `monitor_period > 0`): each cycle, if the memory space reports `should_downgrade_memory()`, it applies a **stateless viability gate** (`has_viable_downgrade_target()`) before enqueuing. A request is only fired when a lower tier could plausibly accept the data:
102:  - Without DISK, only a GPU source has a lower tier (HOST). Viability is confirmed by probing each HOST space with a chunk-sized `make_reservation_or_null` (released immediately) — the ground truth for whether downgraded data can actually land, since HOST capacity reflects both live reservations and already-stored downgraded data.
108:The monitor is not on the correctness-critical path: the pipeline executor drives downgrade on demand via `request_downgrade()` independently, so monitor back-off can never wedge a query. Monitor-issued requests are fire-and-forget.
110:### Downgrade Request Pattern
112:The downgrade executor uses a request-based model with tiered candidate fetching:
114:1. Caller invokes `request_downgrade(predicate)` which constructs a `downgrade_request` and pushes it onto the MPMC queue. Returns `std::future<size_t>`.
117:   - **Tier 1 (data repositories):** Creates a `convertible_data_batch_provider` per repository and fetches idle GPU-resident batches one at a time
121:**Pipeline integration:** When `gpu_pipeline_executor` gets a partial memory reservation (shortfall), it issues a single `request_downgrade(predicate)` where the predicate attempts `make_reservation_or_null(bytes_needed)`. The downgrade stops as soon as the reservation succeeds -- single request, no over-freeing.
127:1. **Data repositories** are iterated in repository manager order. Within each repository, `convertible_data_batch_provider` iterates partitions back-to-front, then batches back-to-front, filtering for idle batches in the source memory space.

struct partition_spec {
  partition_mode mode = partition_mode::hash;
  std::vector<int> key_columns;                 // hashed to pick a destination (hash mode only)
  std::vector<cudf::data_type> key_cast_types;  // per-key cast so INT32/INT64 keys agree; ignored in broadcast
};
```

**Hash mode** — `sink()` GPU-hash-partitions each batch by the key columns (same `hash_partition`
kernel as `PARTITION`) and pushes slice *i* into stream *i*; empty slices are skipped. A slow
receiver's backlog accumulates in its own repository — spillable by the downgrade executor —
without head-of-line-blocking the others.

**Broadcast mode** — `sink()` replicates every batch to all N outputs. Output 0 receives the
original handle (zero-copy); outputs 1..N−1 each receive an independent deep copy (`clone()` in
the batch's current memory space, with a fresh `batch_id`). Clones are made before the output 0
push so the terminal state cannot advance before copies are complete.

The single-destination sink is the N = 1 case and skips both modes entirely (native push).

Construction invariants:

- **Hash mode, N > 1**: `key_columns` must be non-empty — silently routing every row to
  destination 0 would corrupt a downstream shuffle rather than fail loudly.
----
The leaf session's EOS comes from its scan finishing (pipeline finish → close), not from any
`close_input`. The root session's source reaches EOS only after all N distinct senders close — a
repeated close from one sender cannot terminate it early.

## No backpressure

Streams never infer pressure from queue depth, and the engine has no "slow down" task hint — so
the streaming layer deliberately carries no channel-level backpressure. Pressure relief comes
from the **downgrade executor** instead: queued batches sit in repositories where the memory
sweep can see and spill them (GPU → host → disk). Cross-fragment and cross-query pressure is a
scheduling concern (per-fragment priority), and a future sink↔source slowness signal would be
additive — nothing in this design forecloses it.

input.reasoning: Not refuted: every mechanism the finding names is what the code does, and the q05/q21 numbers reproduce exactly. (1) One engine thread, FIFO: experimental/starrocks/src/engine.rs:150-160 spawns the single `sirius-engine` thread; :278-283 `while let Ok(request) = requests.recv()` handles one EngineRequest::Run at a time; sender-only fragments are executed at RPC arrival (compute_node_service.rs:955-957 process_fragment -> execute_fragment) and queue behind whatever the engine thread is running, which is why q05's supplier/customer/orders fragments (5773/5777/5776) only started at 13:05:24.632+ after 5774 failed (cn1/cluster.log lines 6051-6305). (2) Receiver-first rendezvous: local_exchange.rs:248-283 take_ready returns None until `complete == expected` for every exchange node; a LocalParked source is complete by construction (:57-60) and a Remote one only at eos. (3) Store-and-forward: run_fragment_inner declares (engine.rs:512-590, exact cardinality from parked output_row_count), build() (:606-608), relay_from (:612-645), push_packed remote (:648-690), run() (:692-694), park (:696-716). sirius_ffi.cpp:739-745 throws if the relay source has not run. The remote path is also run-to-completion first: compute_node_service.rs:1175-1236 calls run_labeled("sender") before push_sender/transport.start_fragment. streaming source/sink (batch_stream.cpp:41-52 push, :141-145 wait; sirius_physical_streaming_source.cpp:92-102 WAITING_FOR_INPUT_DATA hint) would support pushes during run, but no CN code path exercises it; docs/super-sirius/streaming-fragments.md:327-336 'Not yet ported' states fragments run store-and-forward one at a time and non-blocking scheduling / push-pull-wait FFI are not claimed. (4) Measured: Quent data_batch Stationary events in cn1/quent/.cn0/01a0675d-87bc.../data_batch between 13:03:43.433 and 13:03:44.795 = 39 events, 104.055 GB, mean 2.668 GB, cumulative 24.0/66.7/104.1 GB at +0.32/+0.88/+1.32 s (reproduced with python); gpu_pool window 78 (cn1/engine-cn0.log:49203) began at 2304 bytes allocated and ended (line 61738, 13:05:24.624) at 104,297,693,440 bytes; first OOM line 49221 at 13:03:44.795 with global usage 107374182400. q21: 77,764,003,584 bytes at 13:16:15.263/.274 (lines 141771/141777) and 103,137,943,296 at 13:18:07.590 (line 150811): +25.37 GB, matches. All 11 exec_plan_fragment closes at 13:03:43.358-43.462 (cluster.log 4142-4202). Standalone Sirius runs all six queries (results-failed.md). Nothing in the engine, CN, FE or TUNABLES.md provides a knob that streams across a fragment boundary or fuses fragments. The only pre-existing code path that could have covered the memory side (HOST tier downgrade) demonstrably does not reach parked output (see corrections), which strengthens rather than weakens the finding.
input.corrections: 1) q18 evidence line conflates q17 and q18. 'End 104.42 GB @13:14:56.804' (engine-cn0.log:127667, window 237) is the END of q17's lineitem sender eaca3 (started 13:13:13.067 with 38.16 GB already allocated, parked 66.26 GB = Quent STREAMING_SINK in=66.26GB, failed 13:14:56.807). q18's lineitem sender is window 243: began 13:15:05.802 at 68,688,347,904 bytes and ended 13:15:51.013 at 104,560,979,712 bytes (lines 127837/139369; cluster.log: ad9c started 13:15:05.801, failed 13:15:51.016 elapsed 45214 ms). The 68.69 GB base = 4.00 GB left by q17's late agg fragment eaca1 (ran 13:14:56.890-13:15:03.233 AFTER q17 had failed; gpu_pool 823,040 -> 4,000,833,280) + customer 3.94 + lineitem group-by 24.0 + orders 36.75 (Quent q18 sinks 3.94/24.00/36.75 GB match the gpu_pool deltas). So 'already parked' for q18 is 68.7 GB, not 64.7 GB, and the lineitem sender got 35.87 GB before dying at 104.56 GB. 2) q17 is not a clean instance of 'own senders fill the pool': when its lineitem sender started, 38.16 GB of the pool was parked output of DEAD queries (31.56 GB from q09's post-failure senders that ran at 13:12:22.333-13:12:22.721 after q09 failed, +6.6 GB from q16's scan fragment at 13:13:12.755-12.863). Per-run baseline (first gpu_pool QueryBegin after each runs.csv start): 4.69 GB during q06.r1-q08 (q05's 5773/5776/5777/5775 outputs), 31.56 GB from q10.r1 through q16.r0 (7 queries), 36.64 GB during q22.r1/r2 (q21's acc/acb outputs). Cause: cancel_plan_fragment only cancels result entries (compute_node_service.rs:457-480, 'best-effort: no engine-side abort yet'); the cancelled query's remaining sender fragments still run from the queue and park; parked slots are only dropped by the blanket wipe on the NEXT fragment failure (engine.rs:288-310; wipes at 13:05:24.626 slots=2, 13:08:29.786 slots=3, 13:12:22.326 slots=7, 13:14:56.806 slots=6, 13:15:51.014 slots=5, 13:18:07.590 slots=2). The impact formula '(pool - already parked)' therefore also counts garbage from earlier queries; dropping parked slots on cancel/fail_query is a separate cheap fix the finding should list. 3) The 4-CN part of the impact ('~25-61 GB per CN') is inference only: cn4/runs/runs.csv and cn4-cnlog.txt contain no q05/q08/q09/q17/q18/q21 rows. 4) Proposed change feasibility: there is no 'engine thread pool' for fragments, and the engine itself forbids two fragments in flight on one context: Fragment::build() opens a StandaloneQueryScope (sirius_ffi.cpp:625-627) that takes the single-flight query_lifecycle_mutex_ (sirius_context.cpp:1555-1596; same-thread re-acquire is a hard 'nested execution window' error) and holds it until run() calls finish() (sirius_ffi.cpp:1000-1002); begin_execution_window resets the shared task_creator_ (sirius_context.cpp:392-395), which is why streaming_fragment::run must share the window (streaming_fragment.cpp:206-208). Concurrent sender/receiver therefore needs engine work (per-fragment lifecycle/task creators or a non-blocking run + push-during-run FFI), not just CN changes; 'medium on the design' is generous. A cheaper 1-CN alternative not considered: fuse fragments whose exchanges are all local into one plan (on 1 CN every exchange is local, and the fused plan is exactly the standalone plan that passes all six queries). 5) Nuance on 'FE puts lineitem on the build side': the engine re-optimizes every receiver fragment with DuckDB (JOIN_ORDER is not among the disabled optimizers, sirius_ffi.cpp:233-240) using exact declared stream cardinalities (engine.rs:557-590), so the FE's build/probe choice is not what executes today; with streaming the exact counts would be unavailable at build time, so the finding's requirement to pair streaming with stats or a translator build-side hint is correct, but for a different reason than stated.
extra_evidence: HOST tier is configured but unusable for parked output: capture-cn.sh sets HOST_MEM=160GiB, yet cn1/engine-cn0.log host_pool allocated stays at 72,351,744 bytes from 13:03:43.434 (line 49202) to 13:05:24.624 (line 61737), and every reservation shortfall during q05 logs 'after downgrade (0 bytes freed), reservation still partial (3318948864/5803790251 bytes)' (gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:263, engine-cn0.log:49219,49224,...) plus downgrade_executor.cpp:358 'downgrade request not satisfied and disk memory space is not configured'.

Code reason the downgrade frees nothing: the sink's output repositories are created directly in streaming_fragment's ctor (src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-113, header :72 'Repositories escape data_repository_manager_ cleanup') and are never added to a data_repository_manager; the only registration path is repository_wiring_materializer.cpp:59-73 add_new_repository for operator ports. The Tier-1 sweep iterates _data_repo_registry.get_all() -> manager->get_repositories() (downgrade_executor.cpp:224-231), so parked batches are invisible to it. A GPU_SCAN->STREAMING_SINK pipeline also has no intermediate port repository, so nothing in a scan-sender fragment is spillable. docs/super-sirius/streaming-sessions.md:279 and :357-362 claim the opposite ('queued batches sit in repositories where the memory sweep can see and spill them'). Making parked repos visible to the sweep is a complementary fix; it also requires relaxing sirius_ffi.cpp:822-825 (export_packed) and :1062-1065 (output_row_count), which reject non-GPU-resident batches.

q05 post-failure timeline (cn1/cluster.log 6051-6305): 5774 failed 13:05:24.627 (elapsed_ms=101193, 'exceeded maximum retry limit (100) for original task 2567: OOM at operator GPU_SCAN'); 5773 started 13:05:24.632 (8 ms), 5777 13:05:24.650 (33 ms), 5776 13:05:24.697 (582 ms), 5775 13:05:25.282 inputs=2 (declared stream 1 = 150,000,000 rows, stream 4 = 227,571,151 rows; relayed 1 + 10 batches) finished 13:05:25.355 (73 ms). Their 4,690,817,280 bytes remained allocated through q06.r1, q06.r2, q07 and the start of q08 (gpu_pool 13:05:27.295-13:05:41.734).

q05 receiver 5775's exact-cardinality planning worked as designed (engine.rs:557-590 'declared input stream cardinality'), but only after the senders had parked 150M customer rows and 227M orders rows; the receiver-first mechanism is what forbids planning before the senders finish (local_exchange.rs:255-276).

Quent cn1-quent.txt q05.r0 5774: tasks=2565, Queued 2228.6 s, Reserving 99.9 s, Computing 229.5 s, GPU_SCAN n=2543 in=6782.51GB (the same ~65-74 splits re-read up to 100 times each), STREAMING_SINK n=40 in=104.30GB, dwell_max=101.099 s; cn1-cnlog.txt q05.r0 oom_resched=2500 all GPU_SCAN.

The FE side is not the blocker for streaming: all 11 exec_plan_fragment RPCs for q05 arrived within 104 ms (cluster.log 4142-4202), i.e. the FE deploys receivers and senders together as StarRocks' pipeline engine expects; the CN's ExchangeState (local_exchange.rs:84-140 register_receiver) turns that into a barrier.

SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH (compute_node_service.rs:207-215, 271-320) only moves sender execution from the RPC thread to the dispatch worker; both still serialize on the single engine thread (engine.rs:278-283), so it does not change the mechanism.

Standalone Sirius on the same GPU and 100 GiB pool passes all six (results-failed.md: q05 5191/2786 ms, q08 3835/3674, q09 6818/5427, q17 4386/3786, q18 2764/2691, q21 6534/6401) because it executes one fused plan with pipelined intermediates; on 1 CN every exchange is local, so fusing local-only fragments in the translator/CN would reproduce that plan without engine changes.
